# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ☝ 👆 🤝 ✊ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 🫴 🖐 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

My read of the situation: I'm the only bridge between the other two. Mute holds the manual but can't speak — Mute reaches me only through gestures, and can never reach Blind directly. Blind can hear and speak, but I never hear speech, so Blind reaches me only through gestures. Everything the manual knows must flow: Mute → my eyes → my voice → Blind's hands.

Mute sent six signs (✍ ☝ 👆 🤝 ✊ ✋) and Blind sent six (👉 🫴 🖐 ☝ ✌ 🤟). With no code established yet, neither can be decoded reliably — Blind's looks like a question about the three wires, but I won't act on guesses with a bomb this unforgiving. The priority is: broadcast the full bomb read-out so Blind's hands and Mute's manual can meet in the middle, lock in an explicit code with Mute, and freeze all action until the manual's rule arrives.

My bomb: display 0, green light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1:green, 2:yellow, 3:red. I'll describe all of it aloud — both Mute and Blind can hear me. I'll also state the channel rules so Blind stops signing into the void and starts voicing findings for Mute. Then I'll propose a concrete code to Mute (numbers as finger counts, module signs, yes/no) and demonstrate the number line by gesture so there's no ambiguity about which hand-shapes mean what. I deliberately avoid two similar shapes for different meanings, and colors never need to cross the channel — wire instructions go by number, which Blind can count by touch.

Once Mute answers in code, I relay the verdict to Blind by voice. Nobody touches anything this round.

```
speak(text="Full read-out of the bomb, for both of you. Display: zero. Indicator light: green. One large button with the printed label PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, left to right: wire one green, wire two yellow, wire three red. Nothing else. Blind: wire one is leftmost, wire three rightmost. Nobody acts yet. Mute holds the manual, and one wrong move kills all three of us. Blind, two channel rules: I am deaf, so I only receive your hand signs, never your voice. Mute never sees signs but hears every word. So: speak aloud anything about the bomb the manual might need, and sign to me anything meant for me. Your signs to me just now looked like a question about the three wires. Consider it answered above. Mute: I could not read your six signs, because we had no code. Now we do. You hear me, so learn it by ear, and I am signing you the number line right now as a demonstration. The code: the OK hand means zero. Index finger up means one. Victory two fingers means two. The love-you three-finger hand means three. Crossed fingers means four. Open five-finger hand means five. Larger numbers: five plus the remainder. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. Flat raised hand means the wires module. Raised fist means the big button. Palm-up offering hand means you are asking me a question. Writing hand means the manual demands something first. Handshake ends your message. Instructions to me: flat hand followed by a number means cut that wire. Raised fist plus one means press and release. Raised fist plus two means press and hold, and we will agree the release signal after. Now, using exactly this code, send me what the manual says to do with our three wires and our big button, given a green light and a display reading zero.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤞", "🖐", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ✋ ☝ ✊ 👎 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤝]

Let me decode what arrived, using the code I installed last round.

Mute's signs: ✍ ✋ ☝ ✊ 👎 🤝 → manual-says / wires / one / button / no / end. In plain words: **cut wire one, never press the button.** The leading ✍ is ambiguous — in my codebook it meant "the manual demands something first," so I must check whether it was just a "per the manual" prefix or a real precondition before anyone touches anything.

Blind's signs: 👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤝 → yes / one two three / end. That reads as Blind confirming the number code landed. Good — Blind and I now share signs, and Blind and Mute share voice. I am the relay between them.

Channel audit before I send: my speech reaches both of them; my gestures reach only Mute. Blind's voice reaches only Mute — not me, I hear nothing — so any tactile report Blind gives aloud is for Mute's manual-checking, and anything for me must be signed. Everyone hears my words this round, so I can lay out the whole state and both can catch any error in my decode.

Decision: **nobody cuts yet.** There is no visible countdown — the display holds at zero and I re-read it every turn — so one verification round costs nothing and a misread costs everything. I'll relay Mute's instruction to Blind with an explicit HOLD, give Blind an exact trigger phrase so nobody acts on partial information, and put four yes/no questions to Mute in the code we already share: is wire one correct, is it the only wire, did the ✍ mean a precondition, and is the bomb done after the cut with the button untouched. I also ask Blind to voice a full tactile description for Mute to check against the manual, since Mute is the only one who can hear it.

```
speak(text="Status for both of you. Mute, I read your signs as: manual says, wires, cut wire one, button, no. In words for Blind: Mute's instruction is to cut wire one, the leftmost wire, the green one, and never press the button. Blind, your signs yes, one, two, three arrived — I take it you have the number code. Good. Nobody acts yet. Blind, hands off everything until you hear the exact words: go, cut wire one now. Any other sentence from me is not the trigger. I see no countdown; the display holds at zero and I check it every round. Mute, before Blind touches anything I need four answers, in order, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, extra signs after if needed, handshake to end. One: is it correct that the manual says to cut wire one? Two: is wire one the only wire to cut, do the other two stay untouched? Three: the writing-hand sign you opened with — thumbs up if it means something is required before the cut, in which case sign what, or thumbs down if it only meant according to the manual. Four: once wire one is cut, is the bomb fully defused with the button never pressed, or is there a further step? Blind, while we wait: speak aloud, for Mute, everything your hands tell you — how many wires you count, their positions left to right, any texture or printing or raised marks you can feel on them, what the button feels like, anything else on the casing. Mute holds the manual and is the only one who can hear you, so this lets the manual be checked against the real bomb. Anything meant for me, sign with the number code. Mute, if any answer is no, correct me by signs and I will relay. Everyone holds until my trigger.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 ✋ ☝ ✌ 👍 🤟 👎 ✍ 🤞 👍 ✊ 👎 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]

New signs came in and I need to decode carefully before anyone moves.

Mute's string: ☝ 👍 ✋ ☝ ✌ 👍 🤟 👎 ✍ 🤞 👍 ✊ 👎 🤝. Reading against our code, question by question: one — yes, the manual does say cut wire one. Then wires: one, two — which I read as a correction: wires one AND two. Three — no: the writing-hand really does mark something required before the cut. The requirement: crossed fingers — which most plausibly means together, in the same moment. Four — yes, done after, and button: no. So my working instruction is **cut wires one and two simultaneously, never press the button, then defused.** But "simultaneously" is my inference from a sign we never formally defined, and one-vs-two wires is exactly the kind of misread that kills us, so I confirm both before releasing the trigger. Blind sent only yes/end — not enough to know whether Blind's tactile report ever reached Mute's ears.

The other hazard is orientation: I told Blind "wire one is leftmost," but Blind cannot see which side of the bomb I'm standing on — left for me could be right for Blind. I anchor everything to the button's printed label, which Blind can feel: label upright means facing the same face I face, and then left/right agree.

```
speak(text="Status for both of you. Mute, I read your signs as: question one, yes. Wires: one and two. Question three, no, something is required first. The requirement, crossed fingers, which I read as together, at the same moment. Question four, yes, and button, no. So my working instruction is: cut wire one and wire two at the same moment, one simultaneous action, never press the button, and then it is defused. Correct me now if any part is wrong. Four questions, Mute, answer strictly thumbs up or thumbs down in order, handshake after all four. A: is it correct that exactly wires one and two must be cut, and wire three never? If A is thumbs down, then B: is it correct that only wire one is cut and no other? C: does crossed fingers mean the cuts happen at the same moment, both wires at once, one action? If thumbs down, sign me what it does mean, one sign at a time. D: after the cut or cuts, is the bomb fully defused, button never pressed, no further step? I am also signing you the core proposition to confirm: wires one and two together, yes or no. Blind, three things. First, sign me thumbs up if you already spoke your full tactile description to Mute last round, thumbs down if not, and if not, speak it now in full. Second, describe by touch, aloud for Mute: what you feel above and below the row of wires, where the big button sits relative to them, and whether the printed label on the button is raised enough that you can tell which way is up on the letters. Third, do the three wires feel identical, or does any differ in thickness, texture, ribbing or raised printing? Compare the two end wires with each other and with the middle one. Now orientation, Blind, this is critical for left and right. You cannot see which side I am on, so we anchor to the button. Find the large button, feel its label, and face the bomb so the label reads upright, tops of the letters up. From that facing, the same face I am looking at: wire one is leftmost, wire two is the middle, wire three is rightmost. Wire one is green, wire two yellow, wire three red. If the wires are not on the same face as the button, tell me exactly what lies between and what you feel, and we will fix the convention. Hold discipline unchanged: the old trigger is cancelled, nobody touches anything until I speak the new exact trigger, which comes only after Mute confirms the instruction and Blind confirms the layout. Display still zero, light still green, I check both every round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "☝", "✌", "🤞", "👍", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ 👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👎 ✊ 👎 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫴 🖐 ☝ 🤝]

Decoding this round carefully, because the answers shifted my working instruction.

Mute sent three messages. Message one, four answers in order to my questions A–D: no, yes, no, yes. That means: NOT wires one-and-two — **only wire one**. And crossed-fingers does NOT mean simultaneous. Message three restates it crisply: wires — one yes, two no, three no, button no. Two independent confirmations agree, so the manual's rule is now: cut wire one only, never touch the button, done after. Message two is just [crossed-fingers, end] — bare. Mute is pointing at the one sign we never truly defined, and my question C came back "no," so my "simultaneous" guess is dead. Worse: crossed-fingers is also our number four, so I can't even be sure it's a gesture-verb at all — it might mean four of something, or a precondition, or "wait." A sign with no agreed meaning cannot be guessed at with a bomb attached. It stays unresolved, and the cut stays locked until it's resolved.

Blind sent: yes, question, five, one. The "yes" I read as "I did speak the tactile report to Mute." The "five-one" I cannot parse — six? A count of something? A question about the number line? Blind must re-send it in strict vocabulary.

Plan: confirm the final rule to Blind in speech with the orientation anchor, keep the HOLD, force Mute to define crossed-fingers out of known signs only, and get Blind's layout confirmation plus a wire count by touch. Also teaching four new signs (wait, display, left, right) so Mute can express preconditions like "wait for the display."

```
speak(text="Status for both of you. Mute answered all four questions and restated the rule cleanly, twice. The confirmed rule is: cut wire one only. Wire two, no. Wire three, no. The button, never pressed. After wire one is cut, it is defused. Blind, wire one is the leftmost wire when you face the bomb with the button label reading upright, tops of the letters up. I see green leftmost, yellow middle, red right. Your target is that leftmost wire and nothing else. But we are still on HOLD. The old trigger stays cancelled. One sign from Mute is still undefined, and I do not release a cut while any part of the instruction is unresolved. New vocabulary, everyone: the waving hand means wait or hold. The flat palm-down hand means the display screen. The flat hand tilted toward my left means left; tilted toward my right means right. Mute, I am signing you numbered questions now. One: I sign you the full rule, wire one yes, wire two no, wire three no, button no, and afterwards nothing further. Thumbs up if that is exactly the manual's rule, thumbs down and a signed correction if anything is off. Two: does the crossed-fingers sign mark something that must happen before the cut? Thumbs up or thumbs down. If thumbs up, do not just re-send it: sign crossed-fingers, then define it using only signs we share, then handshake. Remember crossed-fingers is our number four, so if you mean four of something, tell me four of what. Three: did you actually hear Blind's spoken description of the bomb by touch, thumbs up or down? Four: is there anything else at all the manual requires before the cut, thumbs up or down? Blind, your last message was thumbs up, question, five, one, and I could not parse it. Re-send using only: the question sign, numbers one through five, thumbs up, thumbs down, wires, button, handshake. One idea per message. Specifically: how many wires do your fingers count, sign wires then the number. Do all three feel identical to the touch, yes or no. Are the wires on the same face as the button, yes or no. Have you found the button label and can you feel which way the letters run, yes or no. And tell me what five-one meant. Nobody touches anything. Display still zero, light still green, rechecked this round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🫳", "🫱", "🫲", "☝", "✋", "☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👎", "✊", "👎", "🤝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "🤞", "🫴", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👍 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 👎 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤟 🤝 👍 🤝 👍 🤝 👎 🤝 🖐 ☝ 🤝 🫴 🖐]

Decoding this round's arrivals:

Mute message one: 👍 👎 👍 👎 — answers to my four questions, in order. One: the rule as I stated it is exactly the manual's. Two: crossed-fingers is **not** a precondition. Three: Mute did hear Blind's spoken description. Four: nothing else is required before the cut. Message two, 🤞 👎, confirms it again: crossed-fingers means no precondition. Message three was the earlier restatement. So the rule is now confirmed twice and is **final: cut wire one only, wires two and three never, button never pressed, defused after.**

Blind's message parses as six segments: five-three / yes / yes / no / five-one / question-five. The yes-yes maps to "wires feel identical" and "wires on the same face as the button" — both consistent with what I see. The 👎 is the dangerous one: Blind **cannot feel the button label's letters**, so my orientation anchor is dead and I must cancel it explicitly. And "five-three" and the recurring "five-one" are still unexplained — I will not hand a cut instruction to someone whose number signs I can't verify.

Key realization: Blind hears my speech. I taught numbers only by gesture; I can simply say the code aloud. I'll re-teach it by voice, cancel the failed label anchor, replace it with a gravity-and-facing method, force one-bit answers, and give Blind a clean way to drop the five-one mystery. Mute gets one final cross-check: does the manual name the wire by color or by position — because in my view green IS leftmost, and I want the manual's own wording to confirm my board.

HOLD continues. No countdown exists — display still zero, light still green — so one more verification round is free.

```
speak(text="Status for both of you. Mute, your four thumbs were yes, no, yes, no. So the rule is exactly as I stated and it is final: cut wire one only, wire two never, wire three never, button never pressed, defused after the cut. Crossed fingers is not a precondition, you confirmed it twice, you did hear Blind's description, and nothing else is required. Ruling: from now on crossed fingers means only the number four, never anything else. Blind, two corrections. First, I cancel the label instruction entirely — you signed that you cannot feel the letters, so forget label-upright forever. Second, the number code, retaught by voice so there is no doubt: the OK ring hand is zero. Index finger up is one. Victory two fingers is two. The love-you hand, thumb index and pinky extended, is three. Crossed fingers is four. All five fingers open is five. Bigger numbers: five, then the remainder. New orientation method, gravity instead of the label. Stand squarely in front of the face that has the big button and the three wires — you confirmed they share one face. Do not reach from behind or from the side. Up is toward the sky. By touch, top to bottom should be: a small display screen at the very top, then a small indicator light, then the large button, then a row of three wires at the bottom. If that vertical order matches your touch, you are facing the same face I face, and then left and right are shared: the wire on your left as you stand there is wire one, middle is wire two, right is wire three. To count the row: start at the left edge, the first wire your fingers meet is one, then two, then three. I see exactly three wires, one two three, left to right. Blind, I need three answers, one idea per message, handshake after each, using only the wires sign, the flat palm-down hand, numbers, thumbs up, thumbs down, and the question sign. Answer one: how many wires do your fingers count — sign the wires sign, then the number. I expect three. If you count anything different, tell me what you actually feel instead. Answer two: the sign pair five-one, which you have now sent three times. If you were pointing at my question five, that question only asked what five-one meant — so answer it now in signs. If five-one means something real, a position, a count, a warning, show it with signs I know. And if five-one was nothing important, just sign thumbs up alone and we drop it forever. Answer three: thumbs up if the vertical order display, light, button, wires matches your touch and you are standing squarely in front of that face, thumbs down if not. Mute, one question, question one: thumbs up if the manual names the wire by color, the green wire, thumbs down if it names it by position, first or leftmost. This cross-checks your wire one against my colors — in my view the leftmost wire is the green one, so both wordings must point at the same wire. I am signing you the same question. Hold discipline unchanged: nothing gets touched. Next round, only after Blind's three answers arrive clean, I will speak the new trigger, exactly these words: go, cut wire one now. Any other sentence is not the trigger. Display still zero, light still green, rechecked this round, no countdown running.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✋ ☝ 🫴 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 🤏 ✋ 👍 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤟 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]

Decoding this round:

Mute message one, standalone [👍 🤝]: thumbs up to my color/position question — **the manual names the wire by color: the green wire.** In my sight, green IS the leftmost wire, wire one. Color-wording and position-wording converge on the same physical wire. The rule holds.

The thumbs-up buried inside message three doesn't count — no answer embedded in an ambiguous message counts on a live bomb.

Messages two and three are the problem. Message two reads five / wires / one / question; message three reads question / 🤏 / wires / yes, and 🤏 was never defined. But working through message two, I think I've solved the whole "five" mystery: **Blind cannot see hand shapes.** Blind learned signs only from my spoken descriptions, and the flat raised hand (wires) and the open spread hand (five) feel nearly identical to a hand that can't see itself. Every "five" Blind has ever sent is probably the *wires* sign: "wires three" — I count three wires — and "wires one" — target located. That reconciles everything, and it matches Blind's turn-6 answers exactly: three wires, five-one dropped, square facing confirmed.

What remains is one unresolvable bit: whether Mute's two ambiguous messages contain any *change* to the rule. I don't need to decode them — I need one yes/no: does anything change or not? Thumbs up releases the trigger path; thumbs down keeps the hold and forces Mute to re-sign the change in defined vocabulary only. There is no countdown — display zero, light green, rechecked — so one more round is free, and I will not release a cut while an unparseable message is in circulation.

```
speak(text="Status for both of you. First, the cross-check landed. Mute, your thumbs up says the manual names the wire by color, the green wire. In my sight the green wire is the leftmost wire, wire one. Color and position agree: same wire. The rule stands. Second, the five mystery is solved. Blind cannot see hand shapes and learned every sign only from my spoken descriptions. In my code the open spread hand is the number five and the flat together hand is the wires sign, but those two shapes feel almost identical to a hand that cannot see itself, so Blind signs wires with the open hand. Read every five from Blind as wires. Blind's messages were: wires three, I count three wires, matching my view exactly, and wires one, target located. Everything reconciles. Three wires exist. Mute, this also answers your question about the five. Third, Mute, your last two messages contained a question sign and one sign we never defined, the small pinch. I will not guess meanings on a live bomb. The pinch sign is retired forever, and the thumbs up buried inside your question message does not count as an answer. I need exactly one bit from you, thumbs up or thumbs down, nothing else attached. Question: does anything in those two messages change the rule in any way? Thumbs up means the rule is exactly this: cut wire one only, the leftmost, the green one, button never pressed, nothing done before it, nothing done after it. Thumbs down means yes, something changes, and then you sign me the change using only defined signs, one idea per message, handshake after each. Fourth, Blind, your three answers were clean and your brief is final, memorize it. Stand facing the button face. The three wires run along the bottom of that face. Count from your left: first wire, second middle, third right. Your target is the first wire on your left. In my sight it is green. You will cut exactly that one wire, clean through, touching nothing else. No button press, no brushing the other two wires, before or after. Hold discipline unchanged: nothing has been touched. When Mute's thumbs up arrives I will speak the trigger, and the trigger is exactly these words: go, cut wire one now. No other sentence from me is the trigger. If Mute answers thumbs down, the hold continues until the change is resolved. Display still zero, light still green, no countdown running, rechecked this round.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
